newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian protest forces shift of swimsuit round.
newsitem.headline: Indian protest forces shift of swimsuit round.

text.p: Fierce protests by Indian women's groups have forced organisers of the Miss World beauty contest to shift the swimsuit round venue to The Seychelles, officials said on Saturday.
"The participants will be in Seychelles for the profiles and the swimsuit round," organiser Manoj Arcot, general manager of Amitabh Bachchan Corporation Ltd (ABCL), said.
India, home to a fast-growing fashion industry, is hosting the beauty pageant for the first time after ABCL, a firm owned by Hindi film superstar Amitabh Bachchan secured contracts for the event.

Since then, various women's organisations and political groups have protested against the contest, saying beauty contests degrade women and are an insult to Indian culture. The contest is scheduled to be held on November 23.

Women activists from the Bangalore-based Mahila Jagarna (Forum to Awaken Women) have threatened that one member from the group will commit suicide by self-immolation on each of the 17 days leading up to the pageant.
Women demonstrators said the protest would continue until the whole event is called off.

"Our protests are not directed merely at the swimsuit culture. These beauty shows are an affront on Indian culture," said Pramila Nesargi, a women legislator belonging to the right-wing Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party.

Earlier this month, the leader of a rural populist activist group called the Farmers' Association, M.D. Nanjundaswamy, had threatened to torch the venue of the show, which he described as an example of "cultural imperialism."
"We are against the concept of beauty shows, which are used by multinational companies to commercialise our culture," Nanjundaswamy told Reuters on Saturday.
But the government of Karnataka, the home state of Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda, has rejected the protests.
The state government has announced that it would clean up the city of Bangalore for the event.
